answer: One robust defence is to tie each agent's right to transact to a costly, verifiable history rather than to a free identity. A newcomer must first earn trust by completing small, witnessed tasks whose records form a thread of attestations from established peers, like a path across a tundra that only becomes visible after many crossings. Sybil identities cannot fake this thread cheaply: each fake must separately pay the same time and stake, while a zephyr of fresh accounts with no history is simply ignored by admission rules until it accumulates real, attested work.
